solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: One guarding the old sultanate

parts.note: ye is the archaic form of the
Oman is a sultanate on the Arabian peninsula

explanation.surface: A sentry stands watch over some historic Arabian kingdom.
explanation.walkthrough: The Yeomen of the Guard are the Tower of London's ceremonial guards, which is why 'One guarding' fits.
explanation.definitionFit: A Yeoman Warder or Yeoman of the Guard is a member of a royal bodyguard.

clue.text: Fellow went by boat, shortly turning northwards

indicators.note: in a down clue, turning northwards means the letters read upwards, backwards
shortly means the word is cut short, losing its last letter

parts.note: to travel by boat is to sail

explanation.surface: A man made a quick trip on the water heading north.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shortly' trims SAILED to SAILE, and 'turning northwards' reverses that.
explanation.definitionFit: A man's given name stands for any fellow, a common crossword convention.

clue.text: Clubs, say, youngsters renounced without question

parts.note: minors are people under age

indicators.note: without tells us to leave out the letter for question from the word for renounced

parts.note: to quit something is to give it up

explanation.surface: Young people gave up golf or night clubs without asking why.
explanation.walkthrough: In bridge, clubs and diamonds are the minor suits; 'say' marks clubs as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: Clubs is an example of a lower-ranking card group in bridge, alongside diamonds.

clue.text: Observing what faulty bell has?

definitions.meaning: a broken bell makes no ringing sound, read as two words

explanation.walkthrough: The second definition splits the answer as NO TING: a bell that will not ring.
explanation.definitionFit: Noting something means paying attention to it or remarking upon it.

clue.text: Sleeps soundly after school — that's the spirit

indicators.note: after places the sleeps part behind the school abbreviation
soundly signals a word that sounds like the one for sleeps

parts.note: naps are short sleeps

explanation.surface: A pupil dozes deeply once lessons end, and someone cheers them on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that's the spirit' reads as encouragement but defines a strong liquor; 'soundly' gives NAPPS, spoken like NAPS.
explanation.definitionFit: Schnapps is a strong distilled liquor, and spirit is the general term for such drinks.

clue.text: Odd — beauties don't turn out well-dressed

indicators.note: turn out suggests these letters being turned into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Strange that the pretty ones don't appear smartly dressed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Odd' looks like an anagram signal but is part of the fodder; 'turn out' does the rearranging of ODDBEAUTIESDONT.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes someone dressed up smartly and ready to go out.

clue.text: Beverage drunk before prom

indicators.note: before places the word for drunk ahead of the dance

parts.note: high is slang for intoxicated
a prom is a formal dance, a ball

explanation.surface: A drink downed by a teenager ahead of the school dance.
explanation.definitionFit: A highball is a mixed drink of spirits and soda served in a tall glass.

clue.text: An expert's packed protective garment

indicators.note: packed means the expert is stuffed inside the word An

parts.note: a pro is a professional, an expert

explanation.surface: A specialist has stowed away some safety clothing.
explanation.definitionFit: An apron is worn over clothes to keep them clean while cooking or working.

clue.text: Maybe I translated this into French, say

parts.note: I is an example of a part of speech standing for a noun
the French for this is ce

explanation.surface: Perhaps the letter I gets rendered in French, so to speak.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' at the end looks like a filler but is the definition, a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To pronounce a word is to utter it aloud, a synonym of the verb in the clue.

clue.text: Series about one retro English band

indicators.note: about means the series word goes around the other letters

parts.note: a string is a series of things
I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: retro means backward-looking, so the letters for English are read in reverse

explanation.surface: A run of shows featuring a nostalgic English pop group.
explanation.walkthrough: 'band' suggests music but means a finger ring; 'retro' turns the English abbreviation round, and 'about' wraps the series word around that and the one.
explanation.definitionFit: A signet ring is a finger band carrying a seal or crest.

clue.text: Piece English poet neither started nor finished

indicators.note: the poet's name is trimmed, losing both its opening and closing letters

parts.note: Rupert Brooke was an English poet of the First World War

explanation.surface: A poem by an English writer left without beginning or end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Piece' suggests a piece of writing but means a chess piece.
explanation.definitionFit: A rook, or castle, is one of the chess pieces.

clue.text: Alienate troubled sergeant

indicators.note: troubled suggests the letters are disturbed into a new order

explanation.surface: Annoy a worried army NCO and push him away.
explanation.definitionFit: To estrange someone is to make them hostile or distant, the same as alienating them.

clue.text: Outlaw vanished without trace, ultimately? Absolutely right

parts.note: to outlaw something is to ban it

indicators.note: without means the final letter of trace is removed from the word for vanished

parts.note: gone means vanished

indicators.note: ultimately points to the last letter of trace

explanation.surface: A bandit disappeared leaving no sign behind, and that is quite correct.
explanation.definitionFit: The British colloquialism means exactly correct, spot on.

clue.text: Camper usually protects land

indicators.note: protects means the words wrap around and hold the answer within them

explanation.surface: Someone sleeping in a tent normally guards their patch of ground.
explanation.definitionFit: Peru is a country, and land is a common crossword word for a nation.

clue.text: Island in flourishing green and largely cool environment?

indicators.note: in tells us to put the island letter inside the rearranged letters
flourishing suggests the letters being waved about into a new order
largely means most of the word, so the last letter goes

explanation.surface: An island thriving with greenery and cool air: what kind of setting is that?
explanation.walkthrough: 'flourishing' rearranges the colour plus the shortened cool into ECOREGON, and 'in' slips the island letter inside; the question mark admits the definition is loose.
explanation.definitionFit: An ecoregion is an area defined by its ecosystem, so it is a kind of natural habitat.

clue.text: Learners in nearby comprehensive

indicators.note: in places the learners inside the word for nearby

parts.note: around means in the vicinity, nearby
L is the learner-driver symbol, so two learners give LL

explanation.surface: Pupils at a local state secondary school.
explanation.walkthrough: 'comprehensive' suggests a British state school but means wide-ranging.
explanation.definitionFit: Something all-round covers every aspect, so it is broad in scope.

clue.text: Up-and-coming crockery business needs influential organisations

indicators.note: in a down clue, coming up means the letters read from the bottom, in reverse

parts.note: a pot is an item of crockery
CO is an abbreviation for company, a business
something that needs a thing uses it

explanation.surface: A rising pottery firm requires some powerful bodies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Up-and-coming' looks like praise but reverses POTCO to OCTOP.
explanation.definitionFit: Figuratively, an octopus is an organisation with far-reaching tentacles of influence.

clue.text: Pop opera eclipsing a long-running programme

parts.note: pop and pa both mean father

indicators.note: eclipsing means the opera's name hides the letter a within it

parts.note: Norma is an opera by Bellini

explanation.surface: Pop music overshadowing opera in a long-running series.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pop' suggests music but means dad. Panorama is the BBC's long-running current affairs programme.
explanation.definitionFit: Panorama, first aired in 1953, is a famously long-running BBC documentary series.

clue.text: Brief message: retired doctor performs operation

indicators.note: retired means withdrawn, so the whole phrase reads backwards

parts.note: to perform is to act, so performs gives acts

explanation.surface: A short note: the old physician still does surgery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retired' looks like it describes the doctor but reverses all of DRACTSOP.
explanation.definitionFit: A postcard carries only a short note, so it is a brief communication.

clue.text: Youngster needing support on course, beginning in November

parts.note: a tee supports a golf ball on the course

indicators.note: beginning in points to the first letter of November

explanation.surface: A young golfer needs help on the links, starting next month.
explanation.definitionFit: A teen is a teenager, a young person.

clue.text: Nuts and bolts sailors fitted in part of ship

indicators.note: fitted in means the sailors are slotted into the ship part

parts.note: the keel is the spine along a ship's bottom
RN is the Royal Navy, sailors

explanation.surface: Hardware that naval crew install in a vessel's hull.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nuts and bolts' suggests hardware but means essentials.
explanation.definitionFit: The nuts and bolts of something are its essential core, its kernel.

clue.text: Sorted out second part of play for radio?

indicators.note: for radio means the words are heard rather than read, so we take their sound

parts.note: a play's second section could be its scene two

explanation.surface: A broadcast drama's second act has been arranged.
explanation.definitionFit: If something has been seen to, it has been dealt with or fixed.

clue.text: Unusually big weight lifted? Wrong

indicators.note: in a down clue, lifted means the letters read upwards, in reverse

parts.note: OS stands for outsize, unusually large
a ton is a unit of weight

explanation.surface: Was a heavy load raised? Not right.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is a retort meaning that's not true, contradicting a claim.

clue.text: Prove dodgy charity's given too much money

indicators.note: dodgy suggests something unreliable, so the letters shift around

parts.note: aid is help given in charity

explanation.surface: Show that a suspect charity has had excessive funds.
explanation.definitionFit: Overpaid means paid more than one is owed or deserves.

clue.text: Old warriors showing reserve, approaching province

parts.note: ice means reserved coolness of manner
NI is Northern Ireland, often called the Province

explanation.surface: Ancient fighters display reticence as they near a territory.
explanation.definitionFit: The Iceni were an ancient British tribe who rose against Rome under Boudicca.

clue.text: Flag officer on Western Isle

indicators.note: on, in an across clue, puts the officer after the other letters

parts.note: LT is short for lieutenant, an officer

explanation.surface: A flag officer on a western island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flag officer' is a naval rank, but 'Flag' alone is the definition, a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To flag is to droop or tire, just as a plant wilts.

clue.text: Surprised about name I dropped

parts.note: as to means concerning, about
to shed something is to drop it

explanation.surface: Amazed that my name was left off the list.
explanation.definitionFit: Astonished means greatly surprised.

clue.text: Unseemly to make a dash for part of hospital, right away

indicators.note: away means the letter for right is removed

parts.note: to make a dash for somewhere is to run to it
a ward is a section of a hospital

explanation.surface: It is improper to sprint for a hospital ward with nobody to the right.
explanation.walkthrough: 'right away' looks like 'immediately' but removes R from RUN TO, leaving UNTO.
explanation.definitionFit: Untoward means improper or unfavourable, unbecoming.

clue.text: Story about animal

indicators.note: about means the word for story goes round the animal

parts.note: a story can be a lie
an ass is a donkey

explanation.surface: A tale concerning a creature.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines too: the famous collie appears in a novel and films about a dog.
explanation.definitionFit: The collie's tale is a story whose hero is a dog, so the whole clue describes it.
